levels.title: Test smallest even cases
levels.body_md: Your even check looks good for large numbers. Focus on the smallest even weights and whether they can really be split. What is the smallest total you can make from two positive even parts?
levels.question_back: What is the smallest total you can make from two positive even parts?

levels.title: Two parts need minimum sum
levels.body_md: You need two positive even parts, not just one even total. Each positive even part has a minimum size, so their sum has a minimum too. Think about what that minimum sum means for your condition.

levels.title: Line 6 misses lower bound
levels.body_md: The problem is in `L6` with `w % 2 == 0`. It accepts every even number as YES. But the smallest even cannot be written as a sum of two positive evens, so that line needs an extra bound check.

levels.title: Require even and above two
levels.body_md: Two positive even numbers are at least `2` each, so their sum is at least `4`. So you need `w` even and `w > 2` for YES. Your `L6` only checks evenness, so it wrongly says YES for the smallest even. Keep your structure and in `L6` also require `w > 2`. This stays `O(1)` time and memory.
